title: The Effect of Combination Antioxidant Therapy on Reflexion Index (RI), a Measure of Resistance Vessel and Small to Medium Artery Compliance
content: Antioxidants reduce arterial stiffness but the effects previously reported are weak. The effect of 2 weeks of therapy with a combination of antioxidants (l-cysteine, thiamine, pyridoxine and ascorbic acid) on reflexion index, a measure of resistance vessel and small to medium artery compliance, were studied using a Pulse Trace digital photoplethysmography recorder in 40 subjects compared to 38 subjects on placebo. Reflection index fell by -8% (placebo corrected) (95% confidence intervals  -1% to -15%, P = 0.0422) on antioxidant therapy. The reduction in resistance index was positively correlated with increasing age in subjects on antioxidant therapy (r = 0.354, P= 0.0220) but not in subjects on placebo (r = 0.125, P = 0.4520). Resistance index was reduced to a smaller extent than the previously reported -19% (95% confidence intervals -9% to -30%, P=0.0020) reduction in stiffness index (a measure of pulse wave velocity, or central artery stiffness) recorded at the same time (effect size: reflection index = 1.0, stiffness index = 1.5). Combination antioxidant therapy significantly reduced reflection index, but the effect on stiffness index was greater.
